prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro urban railway; CBTC supervises train separation, movement authority (MA), regulation. Actors: Line Traffic Controller (monitors, authorizes changes, directs recovery); Revenue Train Operator (operator interface shows MA limits, speed, location confidence, radio condition; acknowledgements reach Atlas via monitored path rejecting stale commands); field staff; Signal Maintenance Engineer, alias Maple; Cyber Security Officer (access, security events, keys via Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, which supports safety-path authentication and onboard security material under controlled access, no safety-logic change). Elements: Metro Operations Control System, alias Lantern (positions, regulation, alarms; sends Crew Login Token Bundle at duty start). North District Zone Controller, alias Marble (northern main line, turnback, approach to East Junction Interlocking); South District Zone Controller, alias Orchid (southern main line, turnback, approach to West Junction Interlocking); compute MA from location reports, occupancy, field state, send to Atlas; boundary by track ownership, radio overlap, receiving zone reissues MA. East/West Junction Interlockings: vital points/signals; accept only safe commands; indications reach onboard via safety channels. Atlas Onboard Controller, alias Kestrel: active after authentication, energized, valid integrity; checks MA sequence/applicability/consistency; speed enforcement, braking recalculated each cycle; door enable; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log; states: initialization, protected manual, ATO, fallback, cutout; on fast radio degradation falls back to last validated MA, rejecting unverified data. Dual Channel Odometer: divergence degrades mode, raises uncertainty. Propulsion/brake interface isolates non-vital circuits; brake assurance via feedback, pressure, deceleration. Train Radio Modem: maintains Atlas bearer over Wayside Radio Access Network, alias Saffron (overlapping cells in stations, tunnels, crossovers, depot approaches; extra overlap at station throats/interlocking approaches); reports link quality, registration, continuity, quality drops before minimum margin; make-before-break handover. Safety Data Communication Network: vital messages among zone controllers, interlockings, approved interfaces; deterministic routing, monitored latency, authentication; separated from maintenance/passenger traffic; sends Clock Drift Sample Report. Service Timetable Server → Lantern (non-vital). Passenger Information Gateway: non-vital, no safety influence. Voice Dispatch Console: separate, degraded voice. Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges door enable and closed-and-locked with train when berthed. Maintenance Diagnostic Server, alias Quarry:

Document units:
S066: At a zone boundary, the Atlas Onboard Controller confirms train position from the Dual Channel Odometer before accepting the next authority source.
S067: The receiving zone validates route state, train identity, and the expected boundary track section before extending authority beyond the transfer point.
S068: East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking report switch state, track occupancy, and route locking status to the responsible zone controller through vital interfaces.
S069: Wayside supervision compares interlocking indications, train position reports, and radio session state to detect inconsistent conditions before they can affect service.
S070: When the comparison detects a mismatch, the affected authority is withheld or shortened until the condition is resolved under the applicable operating rule.
S071: Metro Operations Control System displays zone status, radio coverage alarms, and train supervision states so that Line Traffic Controller can manage service without direct intervention in vital logic.
S072: Maintenance Diagnostic Server receives non-vital summaries of radio and network health, which allows Signal Maintenance Engineer to investigate degraded coverage trends without connecting to the vital channels.
S073: Wayside Radio Access Network sends the Radio Handover Audit File after each configured reporting interval.
S074: Voice Dispatch Console remains available as an operational communication path, but it is not used as a substitute for safety data messages or zone controller validation.
S075: Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges only the permitted interface indications with the supervising wayside systems, and its state is not allowed to override movement authority logic.
S076: Passenger Information Gateway and Service Timetable Server may receive selected service information, but those non-vital outputs are isolated from the command paths used for train protection.
S077: The CBTC supervision boundary at junctions is defined by the commanded route state, detected point position, and confirmed track vacancy rather than by geographic chainage alone.
S078: East Junction Interlocking is also known locally as Falcon for maintenance callouts and legacy panel references.
S079: North District Zone Controller requests routes through East Junction Interlocking only when the requested path is consistent with the current movement authority and the train approach profile.
S080: South District Zone Controller applies the same route protection principles for interfaces with West Junction Interlocking, including checks on flank protection and conflicting movement locking.
S081: The interlocking retains final vital authority for point movement, point locking, route locking, and release of protected sections.
S082: CBTC supervision treats a route as available only after the relevant interlocking reports points detected, locked, and proved in the required position.
